newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market hedge funds peformed best in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market hedge funds peformed best in 1996.

text.p: Hedge funds specializing in emerging market equity and debt were the top performers in 1996 in the hedge fund category of funds monitored by TASS Management Ltd, a company spokesman said.
"1996 was the year of the emerging market hedge fund," TASS Management chief executive Nicola Meaden said.

"Those (hedge) funds which specialized in equities derived most of their gains from Russian equities, while the debt-oriented funds earned much of their returns from the Latin American, Eastern European and Russian markets."
Emerging market equity funds turned in an average performance of 36.59 percent for the year, while emerging market debt funds posted an average return of 35.07 percent.
European equity and US equity funds were the third and fourth best performers for the year, returning 25.23 percent and 23.18 percent on average, respectively.
Those funds specializing in managed futures were the fifth ranked category, posting an average return of 22.27 percent.

But within the managed futures category, an individual CTA (commodity trading advisor), Dennis Trading Group, topped the overall returns for CTA's and hedge funds in 1996, with a 111.41 pct return, as reported earlier.
Global macro funds earned sixth place, with an average return of 21 percent.
Overall 1996 was a solid year for most hedge funds categories, Meaden said.
The only category which posted a negative return was short sellers which lost an average 3.14 percent for the year.
For the fourth quarter 1996, funds specializing in managed futures topped the performance list, posting average returns of 19.49 percent.
"Managed futures performed brilliantly in the fourth quarter," Meaden said.
"Technically oriented traders did very well and energy, currency, and foreign bond markets provided some of the best trading opportunities."

The second best performing category in the fourth quarter was global macro, with an average 11 percent return, followed by currency funds with 9.02 percent, and European equity funds with 5.89 percent.
Global macro funds benefitted from positions in US stocks, non-US bonds and currency markets, while a strong move by the British pound aided currency managers.
TASS Management Inc is a London-based research company which tracks the performance of about 1,600 "alternative investment" managers and funds globally with $9 billion under management.
"Alternative investments" include hedge funds, CTA programs, managed currency managers, emerging market funds and funds of funds.
